title_en: Supreme People's Court Publishes the Second Batch of Typical Cases on People's Courts Ensuring People's Livelihood
full_text_en:
The Supreme People's Court Publishes the Second Batch of Typical Cases on Safeguarding People's Livelihood

I. Wang Shurong v. He Fuyun, Wang Xisheng, et al. — dispute over right to rural land contractual management

(1) Basic Facts

On October 30, 2007, the Rural Land Contract Arbitration Committee of Taobei District, Baicheng City, Jilin Province ruled that Wang Shurong was entitled to the right to land contractual management over the land cultivated by Wang Zhenxue. The plaintiff at first instance, Wang Zhenxue, then filed a request with the Taobei District People's Court: 1. to confirm that the land contractual management contract signed between the Sanyue Village Committee and Wang Zhenxue was valid; 2. to confirm that Wang Shurong had no right to land contractual management over the land contracted by Wang Zhenxue. Wang Shurong argued in defense that she was entitled to one-fifth of the contractual management right over the land contracted by Wang Zhenxue.

Wang Shurong married on January 25, 1975. Since her husband was a soldier, her household registration remained with Wang Zhenxue's family. In 1982, when the Sanyue Village contracted out the land, Wang Shurong and Wang Zhenxue's family were members of the same household. A family of five contracted 5.4 mu of land, with a per capita share of 1.08 mu. The head of the contracting household was Wang Zhenxue. Wang Shurong's household registration was transferred to Baicheng City in January 1992 and changed to non-agricultural household registration. In the second-round land contracting in 1997, Wang Zhenxue's family contracted 4.82 mu of land and obtained the Certificate of the Right to Rural Land Contractual Management in 2005. Wang Shurong was not recorded as a co-owner.

Wang Zhenxue died in October 2010, and the respondent was changed from Wang Zhenxue to his wife He Fuyun and his sons Wang Xidong and Wang Xisheng.

The court of first instance held: 1. the land contract signed between Wang Zhenxue and the village committee was valid; 2. Wang Shurong did not enjoy a 1.08 mu contractual management right over the land contracted by Wang Zhenxue. The Baicheng Intermediate People's Court, in its second-instance judgment, dismissed Wang Shurong's appeal and affirmed the original judgment. After a retrial, the Baicheng Intermediate People's Court entered a judgment: 1. setting aside the second-instance judgment and item 2 of the first-instance judgment; 2. affirming item 1 of the first-instance judgment. In December 2009, the Jilin High People's Court ruled to reject Wang Shurong's application for retrial. In June 2012, after ordering a retrial, the Jilin High People's Court entered a judgment: 1. setting aside the first-instance, second-instance, and original retrial civil judgments; 2. dismissing Wang Zhenxue's claims.

(2) Judgment

The Supreme People's Court, after ordering a retrial, held that Wang Shurong, as an urban resident, did not enjoy the right to rural land contractual management in the second-round land extension contracting. First, Wang Shurong moved her household registration from Wang Zhenxue's family to the jurisdiction of the Xinli Police Station in Baicheng City in January 1992. Article 26, paragraph 3 of the Law of the PRC on Rural Land Contracting provides: "During the contract period, if the entire household moves into a city with districts and changes to non-agricultural household registration, it shall return the contracted arable land and grassland to the grantor. If the contractor fails to return them, the grantor may take back the contracted arable land and grassland." It can be seen that moving into a city with districts and changing to non-agricultural household registration is a condition for losing the right to rural land contractual management. Since the current law of China does not have explicit and specific provisions on the conditions for an individual rural resident to lose the right to rural land contractual management, it can only be determined by analogy with the most similar provisions in the law. The above provision should become the legal basis for determining whether Wang Shurong was entitled to the contractual management right over the land contracted by Wang Zhenxue's family in the second-round land contracting. At that time, Wang Shurong's household registration had already been moved into a city with districts, and she had become an urban resident; therefore, she should no longer enjoy the right to rural land contractual management. The local second-round land contracting was still carried out in accordance with Article 15 of the Land Contracting Law, with households within the collective economic organization as the unit. The meaning of extension contracting is only to measure the land, without making adjustments. This is in line with the policy of no increase of land when people increase and no decrease of land when people decrease. By then, Wang Shurong was no longer a member of Wang Zhenxue's household, and she did not enjoy the right to land contractual management in the second-round land extension contracting. Second, the Certificate of the Right to Rural Land Contractual Management is an important basis for determining whether a party has the right to rural land contractual management in civil cases.

Wang Zhenxue filed the lawsuit because the ruling by the Taobei District Rural Land Contract Arbitration Committee confirmed that Wang Shurong was entitled to a 0.964 mu land contractual management right in the land contracted by his household. That ruling contained the statement that if the party was dissatisfied, it could file a lawsuit with the court within 30 days. Therefore, the court should accept the case and render a judgment. Furthermore, Wang Shurong did not request the local village committee to contract land to her separately, but claimed that she was entitled to a 1.08 mu contractual management right in the land contracted by Wang Zhenxue's family. Therefore, the dispute over civil rights and interests between equal subjects should not be resolved through administrative litigation. The Supreme People's Court entered a judgment setting aside the retrial judgment of the Jilin High People's Court and the civil judgment of the Baicheng Intermediate People's Court, and affirmed the second-instance judgment of the Baicheng Intermediate People's Court.

(3) Typical Significance

Judging from the four adjudication results of the three-level courts in Jilin Province, some courts had different views on whether to accept civil lawsuits filed by a party on the ground that they enjoyed a contractual management right over land contracted by others, and whether it was possible to determine under certain conditions whether a natural person was a member of a certain rural collective economic organization. This case clarifies that when hearing such cases, courts should determine whether the party enjoys the right to rural land contractual management on the basis of determining whether the party is a member of a certain rural collective economic organization, by analogy with Article 26, paragraph 3 of the Law of the PRC on Rural Land Contracting. Therefore, it has certain guiding significance.

II. Yu Jianshui v. Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited, Shanghai Anshan Road Sub-branch, and Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited, Shanghai Yangpu Sub-branch — dispute over savings deposit contract

(1) Basic Facts

In early May 2008, a third party, Xu, and Chen, an account manager of the defendant ICBC Anshan Road Sub-branch, falsely claimed that the sub-branch was selling one-year fixed-term savings products with an annual interest rate as high as 16%, and lured the plaintiff Yu Jianshui to deposit money at the sub-branch. When handling the account opening procedures, Chen secretly activated online banking for the plaintiff and obtained a U-shield, but only gave the plaintiff a bank card and a current account passbook for wealth management accounts stamped with the seal of the defendant ICBC Anshan Road Sub-branch. The next day, Yu deposited 200 yuan and 500 yuan into the disputed account via an automatic deposit machine and a bank counter respectively. On the 14th of the same month, the plaintiff signed a Power of Attorney with Xu, agreeing that the plaintiff would deposit 25 million yuan with the defendant ICBC Yangpu Sub-branch for a term of one year, with no early withdrawal, no transfer, and no loss reporting. Chen signed the contract in the name of the defendant's agent and, taking advantage of his position, surreptitiously stamped the contract with the business seal of ICBC Yangpu Sub-branch. On the same day, the plaintiff deposited 20.91 million yuan into the above account, and Xu transferred the promised so-called high interest spread of 4.09 million yuan into that account. In the afternoon of the same day, Xu used the fraudulently obtained U-shield to log into the online banking system and transferred and withdrew the 25 million yuan for personal squandering. After the incident, Xu and others were sentenced to criminal punishment by the court for fraud. The plaintiff filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai Yangpu District People's Court on the ground that the deposit certificate had matured and the defendants had failed to pay, requesting the court to order the two defendants to pay the deposit principal of 25 million yuan and corresponding interest.

(2) Judgment

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, in its second-instance judgment, held that compared to ordinary depositors, banks are in a better position to prevent criminals from committing crimes using the bank. Therefore, banks should formulate comprehensive business rules and strictly comply with them to avoid risks as much as possible and ensure the safety of depositors' deposits and protect depositors' lawful rights and interests. However, if the depositor knew in advance that unlawful infringement might occur but failed to take necessary preventive measures, or intentionally violated the necessary security rules and regulations of the savings institution, thereby causing damage to his or her property, and if there is a causal relationship between such fault and the damage result, then the depositor shall bear corresponding liability within the scope of his or her fault.

Chen, as a bank employee, colluded with the criminal Xu, used his work convenience, violated deposit operation procedures, opened online banking for the plaintiff without authorization, and obtained a U-shield and handed it over to Xu. The defendant ICBC Anshan Road Sub-branch had clear fault in staff management, business premise management, and deposit business operation procedures, and this fault had a considerable causal relationship with the fraud of the deposit. Although Yu Jianshui was lured by the fictitious high remuneration of a third party to open an account and deposit at the ICBC Anshan Road Sub-branch, as long as both the ICBC Anshan Road Sub-branch and Yu handled the account opening in accordance with the prescribed account opening procedures, the third party Xu would not have been able to obtain a U-shield linked to Yu's account, nor would he have been able to transfer funds from Yu's account to others without Yu's knowledge. Thus, there was no direct causal relationship between Yu's purpose of depositing money and the fraud of the deposit. Moreover, before the deposit, Yu deposited 200 yuan and 500 yuan into the disputed account via an automatic deposit machine and a bank counter respectively, and after verifying that the amounts were indeed deposited into his account, he then deposited 20.91 million yuan into the account. After the deposit, Yu also always properly kept the passbook, clearly showing that he had fulfilled the duty of reasonable care. Therefore, the savings deposit contract between Yu and the defendant ICBC Anshan Road Sub-branch was lawful and valid, and the bank shall bear the liability to repay the deposit principal and interest to the plaintiff.

Among the 25 million yuan deposited into the plaintiff's account, 4.09 million yuan was deposited by the criminal as high interest paid for the purpose of defrauding control over the plaintiff's account, so this amount should be deducted when the two defendants repay the deposit principal, and interest shall be paid at the corresponding current deposit rate. In a savings deposit contract relationship, after the depositor deposits the money in the bank, ownership of the funds transfers to the bank, and the depositor has a creditor's right to claim principal and interest from the bank based on the savings deposit contract. Therefore, after the criminal defrauds and transfers funds using the depositor's account control, the ownership of the funds recovered in the recovery of stolen property shall belong to the bank. The fact that Yu did not collect the recovered funds does not affect his right to claim against the two defendants based on the savings deposit contract legal relationship. Accordingly, the court ordered the two defendants to repay the deposit principal of 20.91 million yuan and corresponding interest to Yu.

(3) Typical Significance

In recent years, cases where depositors' bank deposits are defrauded by criminals through collusion between internal and external parties and lead to litigation have occurred from time to time. This case is a typical example of a savings deposit contract dispute between a bank and a depositor caused by a bank employee colluding with external parties to lure the depositor into establishing a savings deposit contract with the bank by offering high interest rates for deposits, and then defrauding the depositor's funds. The key to hearing this case lies in determining whether the bank and the depositor were at fault for the loss caused by the fraud, and how to assume liability commensurate with their fault. In this case, the court, taking into account the nature and characteristics of the savings deposit contract, the change in ownership of monetary funds, the bank's performance of its contractual obligations, and the correlation between the plaintiff's fault and the loss result, held that the bank should bear full liability for the depositor's deposit principal and interest loss in accordance with the contract, which better protected the lawful rights and interests of the depositor as a financial consumer, and is of great significance in promoting banks to standardize transaction procedures and strengthen management. The judgment in this case fully reflects and gives play to the normative and guiding role of judicial decisions in the financial market.

III. A/S Dan-Bunkering Ltd. v. Owner of the vessel 'Xingyao' — pre-litigation maritime claim preservation arrest of vessel

(1) Basic Facts

On December 12, 2012, the applicant, A/S Dan-Bunkering Ltd., supplied 485.1820 metric tons of Fol80Cst and 158.5280 metric tons of Gas-Oil of marine fuel to the vessel 'Xingyao', registered in Panama and belonging to the respondent, in the waters of Hong Kong. The cost was USD 461,238.21. The respondent paid only RMB 1,000,000 (equivalent to USD 158,730) and still owed USD 302,508. Subsequently, the vessel sailed into the waters of Shantou, Guangdong Province. The respondent had contacted a buyer and was preparing to deliver the vessel to a new owner. The situation was relatively urgent. In order to prevent the claim from becoming void, the applicant urgently filed a pre-litigation maritime claim preservation application with the Guangzhou Maritime Court on January 22, 2013, applying for pre-litigation arrest of the vessel 'Xingyao' and for an order that the respondent provide security of USD 302,508 or equivalent in RMB. The vessel 'Xingyao' was 225 meters in length, 32 meters in beam, 17.81 meters in depth, and had a deadweight tonnage of 62,343. Due to its large tonnage, it could not berth at the dock, and was anchored approximately 25 nautical miles offshore in Shantou Port. It could depart at any time.

(2) Judgment

After receiving the application, the Guangzhou Maritime Court immediately formed a collegial panel to examine the application. It required the applicant to provide the specific location of the vessel to be arrested. Meanwhile, it prepared the ruling on vessel arrest and the arrest warrant. According to legal provisions, a maritime claim holder shall file a pre-litigation maritime claim preservation application with the maritime court of the vessel's location. In this case, the maritime claim holder provided evidence that the vessel 'Xingyao' had left Hong Kong waters and anchored in the Shantou waters of Guangdong, so the Guangzhou Maritime Court should exercise maritime judicial jurisdiction to arrest the vessel in accordance with the law. The applicant chose to arrest the vessel pre-litigation, and the situation was relatively urgent, meeting the statutory conditions for pre-litigation maritime claim preservation. Upon review, the Guangzhou Maritime Court held that the applicant's application complied with legal provisions and should be granted. In accordance with Article 21, Item 12, Article 23, Paragraph 1, Items 1 and 2, and Article 28, Paragraph 1 of the Special Maritime Procedure Law of the PRC, it ruled to grant the applicant's pre-litigation maritime claim preservation application; arrest the vessel 'Xingyao' belonging to the respondent and berthed at Shantou Port; and order the respondent to provide security of USD 302,508 or equivalent in RMB. On January 24, 2013, the judge took a traffic boat for a round trip of nearly seven hours, braved the sea wind and waves, and boarded and arrested the 60,000-ton class vessel 'Xingyao' at a location 25 nautical miles offshore. After arresting the vessel, the judge actively facilitated negotiations between the applicant and the respondent, and pre-litigation mediation was conducted under the auspices of the court. On January 29, the applicant received full compensation from the respondent.

(3) Typical Significance

This case is a dispute involving parties from different countries, including the Kingdom of Denmark, Panama, and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of China. After the vessel entered the sea area of Guangdong, China, the mainland Chinese court, by exercising judicial jurisdiction in a timely and effective manner to arrest the vessel before litigation and conducting pre-litigation mediation, efficiently resolved the dispute between the parties in only five days, truly achieving 'case concluded, matter settled'. On March 26, 2013, the Guangzhou Maritime Court received a letter from the applicant expressing gratitude for the Chinese court's timely and efficient arrest of the vessel to resolve the dispute.

This case set three records for the Shantou Tribunal of the Guangzhou Maritime Court: 'largest tonnage of foreign vessel arrested', 'farthest offshore distance for a shipboard arrest', and 'shortest time to resolve a dispute'. The timely and effective arrest of the vessel was a crucial way for the foreign party, which came to a Chinese court for litigation for the first time, to safeguard their rights, and a window to truly experience the credibility of Chinese judiciary. The successful resolution of this case demonstrates the significance of the Chinese maritime judiciary's 'implementation of a quality strategy to create first-class brands', enhances the trust of foreign parties in Chinese maritime justice, and is conducive to establishing the judicial credibility of Chinese courts and the good judicial image of judges.

IV. Shanghai Hegu Biotechnology Co., Ltd. v. Shanghai Administration for Industry and Commerce — dispute over administrative penalty decision

(1) Basic Facts

Starting from September 2011, the plaintiff Hegu Company purchased six varieties of 'Flower Flag' series health foods, such as 'Flower Flag · Jinzhu Kang', from Sangang Company at a price of RMB 60 per box (after January 2012, RMB 65 per box) for sale in the Shanghai area. In the course of business, the plaintiff collected a large number of private phone numbers in Shanghai, targeting elderly people aged 60 and above. It required employees to use pre-designed scripts containing deception, such as 'Tourism Talk', which were uniformly designed and produced by the company. It invited elderly people to participate in free tourism activities organized by the company under the false names of US Citigroup, Citibank, etc. It also falsely claimed that US Citigroup was established in 1832, and played videos or ppt materials promoting the therapeutic effects of 'Flower Flag' series products. During the sales meeting process, the plaintiff arranged employees without medical qualifications to take pulses of the elderly on site under the guise of 'traditional Chinese medicine', and correspondingly 'diagnosed' the elderly's diseases one by one based on the diseases reflected in the 'US Flower Flag Tourism Application Survey Form' that the company had previously required the elderly to fill out, and took the opportunity to sell 'Flower Flag' series health foods to the elderly at a price of RMB 898 per box (before February 2012, RMB 798 per box). According to a special audit by Shanghai Gongxin Zhongnan Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd., Hegu Company's total sales from September 2011 to September 2012 were RMB 20,532,458; after deducting product procurement and marketing costs totaling RMB 16,891,096.13, refunds to consumers of RMB 2,365,535.00, and related taxes and fees of RMB 12,795.92, the illegal gains amounted to RMB 1,263,030.95.

The Inspection Brigade of the Shanghai Administration for Industry and Commerce (hereinafter referred to as 'the Inspection Brigade') issued an administrative penalty decision against Hegu Company on June 18, 2013. It found that the above actions constituted fraud. In accordance with the provisions of the Shanghai Consumer Protection Regulations, it decided to impose the following penalty on the party: confiscate illegal gains of RMB 1,263,030.95; impose a fine of one times the illegal gains, i.e., RMB 1,263,030.95; total penalty of RMB 2,526,061.90. It also informed the party of the right to appeal and the time limit for filing a lawsuit. The plaintiff believed that the penalty should be based on the provisions concerning false advertising in the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Thereupon, it filed an administrative lawsuit with the Shanghai Xuhui District People's Court, requesting the court to set aside the administrative penalty decision issued against it.

(2) Judgment

The Shanghai Xuhui District People's Court held that the focus of dispute in this case was the application of law, i.e., whether the plaintiff's conduct constituted 'fraud' or 'false advertising'. Article 22 of the Shanghai Consumer Protection Regulations provides: 'When providing goods or services, business operators shall not use fraudulent methods such as passing off fakes as genuine, selling inferior goods, selling adulterated goods, or falsely pricing to damage the lawful rights and interests of consumers. The fraud referred to in the preceding paragraph means the intentional act of informing consumers of false information or intentionally concealing the true situation to induce consumers to make a wrong expression of intent.' It can be seen that 'consumer fraud' is defined by enumeration plus a catch-all clause. In addition to the four explicitly listed fraudulent methods, as long as the method used by the merchant meets the requirements, it can be identified as consumer fraud. In this case, in the activities organized by the plaintiff targeting elderly consumers, which were called free tours but were actually sales meetings, the plaintiff made false propaganda about the efficacy of 'Flower Flag' series health foods, and promoted the 'Flower Flag' series health foods by methods such as impersonating Chinese medicine 'pulse diagnosis', all of which met the definition of fraud in the law. Viewed in isolation, each fraudulent method might constitute false advertising, illegal advertising, etc., as provided in the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the PRC, the Advertising Law of the PRC, etc., but the above methods and means were closely linked and ultimately constituted a complete consumer fraud. Furthermore, the identification of fraud focuses on protecting consumers' lawful rights and interests, while the identification of false advertising focuses on the rights and interests of other competitors, and does not require a wrong decision by the consumer as a prerequisite. In summary, the challenged administrative penalty was based on clear facts, correct application of laws and regulations, and lawful procedures. Accordingly, the court of first instance entered a judgment upholding the decision.

After the judgment of the first instance, Hegu Company disagreed and filed an appeal with the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court. During the second instance, it voluntarily withdrew the appeal.

(III) Typical Significance

The people's court legally supports the industrial and commercial authorities in rectifying the market economic order and effectively safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of consumers. At the same time, through legal reasoning and analysis, it made Hegu Company aware of the illegality and punishability of its actions, prompting it to voluntarily correct its conduct and withdraw the appeal, thereby truly achieving the resolution of the case and the settlement of the matter.

According to statistics, China's annual health product sales amount to RMB 200 billion, with elderly consumers accounting for over 50% of the total. In an era of increasing aging, the elderly population is growing rapidly, and their ability to discern is relatively weak, so their legitimate rights and interests deserve the attention and protection of the whole society. This case is an administrative case in which an industrial and commercial authority imposed a penalty for consumer fraud in the guise of tourism and the promotion of health products to the elderly. In the first instance, the deputy director of the Shanghai Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce, the defendant, appeared in court to respond to the lawsuit. The court's judgment in court effectively deterred the violator and promoted the creation of an honest environment. After the judgment, CCTV's "Focus Interview" and "Weekly Quality Report," as well as Shanghai's "Xinmin Evening News" and "Shanghai Legal News," all reported on the case. Through the "extended effect" after the judgment and extensive publicity, the chaos in the health product market was effectively exposed, and the case also reminded elderly consumers to be vigilant against various types of fraud, achieving an organic unity of social and legal effects.

V. Wuhan Huazhen Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. v. Wuhan Municipal People's Government, Wuhan Municipal Bureau of Land Resources and Planning, Wuhan Jinfu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., and Wuhan Hanqiao Zhongxing Group Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Land Administrative Confirmation

(I) Basic Facts

The disputed land in this case was originally owned by Wuhan Hanqiao Zhongxing Group. In 1996, it leased the buildings constructed on the land to Huazhen Company for use. After Huazhen Company completed the relevant procedures, it obtained the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" No. Wuguoyong (2004) 2732. On November 21, 2004, Hanqiao Zhongxing Group, using Huazhen Company's name, signed the "Land Transfer Agreement" with Jinfu Company. The Wuhan Municipal People's Government cancelled the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" No. Wuguoyong (2004) 2732 on December 29, 2004, and issued the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" No. Wuguoyong (2004) 2910 to Jinfu Company on December 30 of the same month. Subsequent identification proved that the seal of Huazhen Company and the signature of its legal representative "Qian Weiguo" submitted by Jinfu Company when applying for the certificate were different from those retained in the industrial and commercial administration department. On February 1, 2007, upon Jinfu Company's application, the Wuhan Municipal People's Government changed the use of the disputed land from the original industrial use to urban mixed residential use. On February 10, after public announcement by the land department, the Wuhan Municipal People's Government issued the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" No. Wuguoyong (2007) 162 to Jinfu Company on March 12, 2007. Huazhen Company, dissatisfied with the actions of the Wuhan Municipal Government and the Wuhan Municipal Bureau of Land and Resources in cancelling the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" No. Wuguoyong (2004) 2732 and issuing the "State-owned Land Use Certificate" No. Wuguoyong (2004) 2910 and No. Wuguoyong (2007) 162, filed an administrative lawsuit on January 2, 2008.

(II) Judgment

The Hubei High People's Court, in the second instance, held that during the process of handling the registration of change of land ownership, the Wuhan Municipal People's Government and the Bureau of Land and Resources failed to exercise careful review obligations. Without Huazhen Company, the land transferor, submitting a written application for change of registration, lacking the identity certificates of the legal representatives of both the transferor and the transferee, and under circumstances where the company seal and the signature of the legal representative were suspected of being forged, they still transferred the land use right registration to Jinfu Company and cancelled Huazhen Company's land use right certificate. This act violated legal procedures and was not lawful. Accordingly, the second-instance court upheld the judgment of the Wuhan Intermediate People's Court confirming the illegality of the sued administrative act.

(III) Typical Significance

This case went through several trials, affected the interests of multiple parties, and had complex facts. Moreover, since filing the lawsuit, the plaintiff Huazhen Company had long organized personnel to engage in petitioning activities at the court and the people's government. The Wuhan Intermediate Court and the Hubei High Court strictly adjudicated the case according to law, submitted only to the facts and the law, and were impartial and incorruptible. The presiding judge withstood pressure and organized multiple mediations. After the judgment, the court proactively sent a judicial suggestion letter to the government, avoiding adjudicating the case in isolation and extending the trial function. Ultimately, through post-judgment mediation and settlement, the rights, interests, and ownership of the disputed land were resolved at once. The judgment in this case has positive guiding significance for how government agencies handle the registration of change of land ownership in accordance with the law. At the same time, it fully reflects the important function of administrative trial in supervising the government to administer according to law and protecting the interests of the counterparties.

VI. Hao Longzhi et al. (15 persons) v. Tunliu County People's Government — Dispute over Failure to Perform the Statutory Duty of Public Announcement of Land Expropriation Plan and Land Expropriation Compensation and Resettlement Plan

(I) Basic Facts

The plaintiffs, Hao Longzhi and 14 others, and the third parties, Gao Anxi and 5 others, are all villagers of Wanggongzhuang Village, Ligao Township, Tunliu County. In 1991, Hao Yiming, Gao Anxi, and others signed land contract contracts with Wanggongzhuang Village, contracting the village's orchard land, with the contract term from 1993 to 1999. After the contract expired, it became a one-year renewal until 2003. In October 2003, the orchard land contracted by Hao Longzhi, Gao Anxi, and others was occupied by Changzhi Dekai Yafei Automobile Chain Sales Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Dekai Company"). On November 24, 2004, the Tunliu County People's Government submitted a "Request for Instructions on the Land Use for the Renovation and Expansion Project of Halal Meat Deep Processing of Changzhi Dekai Yafei Automobile Chain Sales Co., Ltd." to the Shanxi Provincial People's Government and the Changzhi Municipal People's Government, applying for the expropriation of 6.7293 hectares of land in Wanggongzhuang Village, including 0.57 hectares of arable land and 6.1593 hectares of orchard land. The orchard land contracted by Hao Longzhi, Gao Anxi, and others was within the scope of the proposed expropriation in the request. On December 14, 2005, the Tunliu County People's Government signed a "Land Compensation Agreement" with Wanggongzhuang Village, stipulating that the Tunliu County People's Government would use 100 mu of land from Wanggongzhuang Village, with the compensation fee paid in installments each year, at RMB 50,000 per year (RMB 500 per mu). On August 4, 2006, the Shanxi Provincial People's Government approved the expropriation of the above land with Document Jin Zheng Di Zi [2006] No. 285, and the Tunliu County People's Government was responsible for the supplement of arable land for the converted area, post-approval implementation, and public announcement. Starting from 2004, the Tunliu County People's Government paid Hao Longzhi, Gao Anxi, and others a land rental fee of RMB 500 per mu each year through Wanggongzhuang Village until 2008. In 2009, due to Hao Yiming, Gao Anxi, and others filing this lawsuit, Wanggongzhuang Village did not distribute the land rental fee to the contracting households.

In June 2007, the Tunliu County Bureau of Land and Resources transferred the expropriated 6.7293 hectares of land to Dekai Company for the renovation and expansion project of Halal meat deep processing. On August 27 of the same year, the Tunliu County Bureau of Land and Resources publicly announced the review of the initial registration of this land. Hao Longzhi, Gao Anxi, and others claimed that they only learned at that time that the contracted land had been expropriated and transferred to Dekai Company. The Tunliu County Government had never informed them of the land expropriation from the beginning and had not performed its statutory duty of public announcement of the land expropriation plan and the compensation and resettlement plan. Instead, it had been compensating them in the form of land rental fees. Therefore, they filed a lawsuit, requesting that the Tunliu County People's Government perform its duty of public announcement in accordance with the law and pay the land expropriation compensation in a lump sum.

(II) Judgment

The Changzhi Intermediate People's Court in the first instance held that on December 14, 2005, the Tunliu County People's Government signed a land compensation agreement with Wanggongzhuang Village, stipulating an annual payment of land compensation to Wanggongzhuang Village. Hao Longzhi, Gao Anxi, and others had already received compensation from the village committee, which should be considered as their acceptance of the land compensation and resettlement plan. Therefore, the public announcement of the land compensation and resettlement plan would have no practical significance, and Hao Longzhi et al.'s claim for the Tunliu County People's Government to perform its duty of public announcement of the compensation and resettlement plan should be dismissed. In August 2006, with the approval of the Shanxi Provincial People's Government, the land was converted to construction land. Hao Longzhi, Gao Anxi, and others had already known that the land was expropriated and used by Dekai Company. The public announcement of the land expropriation plan by the Tunliu County People's Government would also have no practical significance. Therefore, Hao Longzhi et al.'s claim for the Tunliu County People's Government to perform its duty of public announcement of the land expropriation plan should also be dismissed. Accordingly, in accordance with Article 56, Paragraph (4) of the "Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," the court ruled: Dismiss the claims of the plaintiffs Hao Longzhi and the other 14 persons.

The Shanxi High People's Court in the second instance held that, according to the relevant provisions of the "Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China" and the "Regulations for the Implementation of the Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China," when the state expropriates land, it shall perform the statutory duty of public announcement of the land expropriation plan and the land expropriation compensation and resettlement plan in accordance with legal procedures. The "Measures for the Announcement of Land Expropriation" of the Ministry of Land and Resources provide detailed provisions on the matters to be announced. Article 4 stipulates: "The people's government of the city or county where the land to be expropriated is located shall, within 10 working days from the date of receiving the approval document for the land expropriation plan, make a public announcement of the land expropriation plan. The land administrative department of that city or county people's government shall be responsible for the specific implementation." Article 7 stipulates: "The land administrative department of the relevant city or county people's government, in conjunction with the relevant departments, shall, within 45 days from the date of the public announcement of the land expropriation plan, formulate a land expropriation compensation and resettlement plan based on the approved land expropriation plan, taking the owner of the expropriated land as the unit, and make a public announcement." Article 14, Paragraph 1 stipulates: "If a public announcement of the land expropriation plan is not made in accordance with the law, the expropriated rural collective economic organization, rural villagers, or other right holders have the right to request a public announcement in accordance with the law and have the right to refuse to go through the formalities for registration of land expropriation compensation. If a public announcement of the land expropriation compensation and resettlement plan is not made in accordance with the law, the expropriated rural collective economic organization, rural villagers, or other right holders have the right to request a public announcement in accordance with the law and have the right to refuse to go through the formalities for compensation and resettlement." In this case, on August 4, 2006, the Shanxi Provincial People's Government approved the conversion of the disputed land to construction land and the completion of expropriation procedures, and designated the Tunliu County People's Government to be responsible for post-approval implementation and public announcement. After receiving the land expropriation approval document from the Shanxi Provincial People's Government, the Tunliu County People's Government organized the implementation of the expropriation work and the transfer work, but did not perform its duty of public announcement and did not handle the compensation and resettlement procedures in accordance with the law. The land rental fees paid by the Tunliu County People's Government to the appellants Hao Longzhi et al. starting from 2004 cannot be equated to the compensation and resettlement fees for land expropriation. The appellants Hao Longzhi and the other 14 persons, as expropriated rural villagers, have the right to demand that the Tunliu County People's Government perform its duty of public announcement of the land expropriation plan and the land expropriation compensation and resettlement plan, and pay the land expropriation compensation and resettlement fees in accordance with the law. The original judgment's view that the expropriation had already been completed and that Hao Longzhi et al. had received land rental fees, which should be considered as acceptance of the compensation and resettlement plan, and that the Tunliu County People's Government's performance of the duty of public announcement of the land expropriation had no practical significance, cannot be sustained. In summary, the reasoning and result of the original judgment were improper, and this court hereby corrects them in accordance with the law. Pursuant to Article 61, Paragraph (2) of the "Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," the judgment is as follows: 1. Revoke the administrative judgment (2009) Chang Chu Xing Chu Zi No. 007 made by the Changzhi Intermediate People's Court on December 9, 2009; 2. The Tunliu County People's Government shall perform its duty of public announcement of the land expropriation plan and the land expropriation compensation and resettlement plan in accordance with the law.

(III) Typical Significance

In land expropriation, the administrative organ is both the decision-maker and the executor, with highly concentrated power and a great risk of abuse. Therefore, the system design should strive to ensure the open and fair operation of power, increase the transparency of land expropriation, and protect the expropriated persons' right to know and the right to submit opinions, so as to regulate expropriation behavior. The land expropriation announcement system, including the public announcement of the land expropriation plan and the public announcement of the land expropriation compensation and resettlement plan, is a legal procedure to ensure the expropriated farmers' right to know, and is a procedural safeguard for the transparency of the expropriation and compensation and resettlement work. The "Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China," the "Regulations for the Implementation of the Land Administration Law of the People's Republic of China," and the "Measures for the Announcement of Land Expropriation" of the Ministry of Land and Resources clearly stipulate the content, form, and procedures for the public announcement of land expropriation. In addition, Article 19 of the "Provisions on Hearings on Land and Resources" of the Ministry of Land and Resources, which came into effect on May 1, 2004, stipulates that when formulating the compensation standards and resettlement plans for the proposed expropriation project, the competent department shall, before submitting for approval, inform the parties of their right to request a hearing. Articles 10 to 12 of the "Regulations on Open Government Information," which came into effect on May 1, 2008, stipulate that the people's governments of cities and counties and their departments, as well as township people's governments, shall focus on disclosing government information such as the expropriation of land and the distribution and use of compensation and subsidy funds. This can be said to be a new requirement and important supplement to China's land expropriation announcement system. In practice, if, during the expropriation process, the administrative organ fails to perform its duty of public announcement of the land expropriation in accordance with the law, depriving the expropriated farmers of their right to know about the expropriation and their right to a hearing and to submit suggestions on the expropriation compensation and resettlement plan, it means that the expropriation procedure is seriously illegal. The expropriated farmers have the right to file a lawsuit with the people's court, requesting that the administrative organ perform its duty of public announcement of the land expropriation in accordance with the law. In this case, although the expropriation had already been implemented, the expropriated farmers had been unaware of the expropriation throughout. After trial, the people's court found that the administrative organ had not performed its duty of public announcement of the land expropriation, and directly ordered the administrative organ to perform its duty of public announcement of the land expropriation. This effectively promoted the administrative organ to administer according to law and protected the legitimate rights and interests of the expropriated farmers. After the judgment became effective, the Tunliu County People's Government attached great importance to it, established a leading group for enforcement, actively implemented the judgment, reached a compensation agreement through consultation with the expropriated farmers, and the land expropriation compensation of RMB 3,929,310 was fully paid. Hao Longzhi and the other 14 persons have submitted a "Request for Withdrawal of Enforcement Application" to the Changzhi Intermediate People's Court.

VII. Liu Yongquan et al. (11 persons) v. Inner Mongolia East Power Co., Ltd., Xing'an Electric Power Bureau — Labor Dispute

(I) Basic Facts

In 1993, the State Council formulated the "Provisions on the Placement of Surplus Employees of State-owned Enterprises," and state-owned enterprises began to place surplus employees. Between 2000 and 2003, the Xing'an Electric Power Bureau signed "Agreements on Leaving Posts for Rest and Retirement" with eleven employees including Liu Yongquan. The agreements stipulated: After going through the formalities for leaving posts for rest and retirement, employees shall not return to work posts; they are considered on the roster, and the unit shall pay a living allowance; during the period of leaving posts for rest and retirement, floating wages and bonuses are cancelled; except for enjoying general wage adjustments, they shall not enjoy other wage policies for increasing wages; welfare benefits shall be implemented at 50%; pension, medical, housing, unemployment and other benefits shall be treated as those for on-the-job employees of the unit; seniority shall be calculated continuously; and formal retirement procedures shall be completed upon reaching the legal retirement age.

After the restructuring of the Xing'an Electric Power Bureau, it overcame difficulties. For on-the-job employees, the wage structure was adjusted and the amount increased. The eleven persons including Liu Yongquan believed that they should enjoy the general wage adjustments of the on-the-job employees of the unit in accordance with the agreements on leaving posts for rest and retirement. Since the wage structure had changed, the increases in wages of on-the-job employees should all be considered as general wage adjustments. Therefore, they filed a lawsuit with the people's court, requesting that the Xing'an Electric Power Bureau be ordered to pay back wages including seniority wages, efficiency wages, position efficiency wages, position base wages, position grade difference wages, and position wages, totaling RMB 601,500.

(II) Judgment

After going through the first instance, second instance, and two retrials, the Inner Mongolia High People's Court held that the dispute between the parties should be resolved by the relevant departments under the policies for enterprise restructuring, and did not fall within the scope of labor disputes that the people's court should accept, and ruled to dismiss the lawsuit. The Supreme People's Procuratorate filed a protest, and the Supreme People's Court conducted a retrial.

The Supreme People's Court, in the retrial, held that this dispute arose during the process of reforming China's state-owned enterprise system and labor employment system. In 1993, the State Council promulgated the "Provisions on the Placement of Surplus Employees of State-owned Enterprises," which made principled provisions on the conditions, procedures, and living allowances for leaving posts for rest and retirement. The purpose was to enhance the vitality of enterprises and improve their economic efficiency through reform, while also properly placing surplus employees of state-owned enterprises and ensuring their basic living. The signing of the agreements on leaving posts for rest and retirement between Liu Yongquan and the other eleven persons and the Xing'an Electric Power Bureau had the nature of implementing the above reform measures. In particular, the Xing'an Electric Power Bureau made specific commitments in the agreements on leaving posts for rest and retirement, such as the enjoyment of general wage adjustments by those who left posts for rest and retirement. This reflected a consensus reached between the workers and the employer on wage treatment, which was not inconsistent with Article 47 of the "Labor Law of the People's Republic of China," which provides that "the employing unit shall, based on the characteristics of its production and operation and its economic efficiency, independently determine the wage distribution method and wage level of the unit in accordance with the law." It contained elements of a labor relationship, and the dispute in this case was a labor dispute, which the people's court should accept. Among the claims of the parties, except for the position efficiency wage of RMB 99,840, which was of a bonus nature and should not be enjoyed according to the agreement on leaving posts for rest and retirement, the rest should be regarded as general wage adjustments within the system and should be supported. Therefore, the judgment ordered the Xing'an Electric Power Bureau to pay back wages of RMB 501,660 to the eleven persons including Liu Yongquan.

(III) Typical Significance

This case is of strong typical significance in accurately determining which disputes arising from enterprise reform are labor disputes and in allowing both parties in the labor relationship to seek protection of their legitimate rights and interests through litigation. During the development of China's socialist market economy, the important reform measures formulated by the State Council must be strictly implemented. The agreements on leaving posts for rest and retirement contain elements that implement the policies for the reform of state-owned enterprises. Such issues indeed need to be resolved by the relevant departments in a coordinated manner according to the policies for enterprise restructuring. However, the agreements also contain content in which the employer and the worker determined wage treatment through agreement, such as the commitment that employees who left posts for rest and retirement would enjoy general wage adjustments. Wages are an important component of labor contracts. The content determining wage standards has the nature of a labor contract. When a dispute arises over whether wages have been paid in accordance with the labor contract, after going through the legal procedures and filing a lawsuit, the people's court shall accept it.

This case is also of typical significance in properly handling situations where an employer, citing its legal right to independently determine employee wages, defends against an employee's wage claims. In the off-post early retirement agreement, the agreement that Liu Yongquan and the other ten persons would receive general wage adjustment treatment, although it did not directly specify a definite wage amount, was a wage standard determined by both parties through negotiation. This is also a specific method for the unit to determine wages, and it is consistent with the spirit of the Labor Law that the employer has the right to independently determine employee wages; in fact, the two are not contradictory. Once the wage standard is determined, in the absence of an agreement or a change in circumstances provided by law, the agreed wage standard must be performed. Liu Yongquan and the other ten persons, in order to alleviate the burden on the state-owned enterprise and increase its vitality, took the overall situation into consideration and made contributions and sacrifices for the enterprise's development by taking off-post early retirement. After leaving their posts, they received basic living expenses for a long period and faced financial difficulties. Most of their claims were merely for the wage content agreed in the agreement. When the enterprise's operations improved, these employees who lawfully asserted their rights should share the reform achievements together with the employees still on active duty. Apart from the wage benefits explicitly excluded in the agreement, their reasonable demands should be satisfied.

The Supreme People's Court's judgment supported the reasonable and lawful part of the claims of Liu Yongquan and the other ten persons. Through the trial, it restored the true facts, gave the employees the justice they deserved, and effectively protected the lawful rights and interests of the workers.

VIII. Series of Cases on Disputes over Crew Labor Contracts Involving the "Misimu" Vessel

(1) Basic Facts

The "Misimu" vessel is a bulk carrier owned by Misimu Shipping Company, registered at the port of Willemstad, Netherlands Antilles. In June 2012, the vessel accidentally collided with another vessel while navigating in China's coastal waters. The accident caused severe damage to the other vessel and also resulted in an oil spill due to the collision, polluting the nearby sea area. After the accident, the "Misimu" was sent to Chongming dock for repairs. From that time onward, wages for 11 Ukrainian crew members on board were not paid. Later, 6 crew members paid their own way to return home first, while the remaining 5 crew members stayed on board to guard the vessel. In July 2013, the 5 Ukrainian crew members still on the "Misimu" filed a maritime preservation application with the Shanghai Maritime Court for the arrest of the vessel due to the shipowner's long-term wage arrears, and filed lawsuits against the shipowner Misimu Shipping Company for disputes over crew labor contracts.

The Shanghai Maritime Court accepted the cases promptly. The departments for case filing, trial, and enforcement performed their respective duties and cooperated closely, properly handling the series of disputes involving the "Misimu" through three measures. First, unity and cooperation to guide the crew members in litigation. Judges from the filing, trial, and enforcement departments boarded the vessel together to carry out the arrest. Considering that the foreign crew members were not familiar with China's judicial system and that traveling between the vessel's anchorage and the court was quite inconvenient, the judges from each department, taking the opportunity of boarding the vessel for the arrest, provided guidance to the crew members according to their respective responsibilities on the risks of arrest and litigation, and on the phases of filing, trial, and enforcement. They patiently and thoroughly answered the crew members' questions regarding the collection of evidence and service of litigation documents, guiding them to assert their rights lawfully and preparing for the efficient trial of the relevant cases. Second, overall planning to coordinate the connection between the filing, trial, and enforcement procedures. Considering the litigation situation of the "Misimu", the crew members' wages were likely to be satisfied through the auction of the vessel. To ensure the timely and smooth transfer of the "Misimu" after auction, the filing, trial, and enforcement departments actively conferred and proposed corresponding response plans for potential issues such as the claims of crew members who had already left the vessel, the advancement of repatriation costs for foreign crew members on board, and the handover of the vessel after foreign crew members left the vessel during the arrest period. At the same time, they exchanged information, cooperated, advanced work simultaneously, and explained matters to the parties, effectively safeguarding the rights and interests of all parties and striving for the best processing results. Third, vessel auction to ensure the priority compensation of crew wages. Upon the application of the parties, the enforcement department lawfully conducted a public auction of the "Misimu". Due to the downturn in the shipping market, vessel auctions had become increasingly difficult in recent years. Enforcement judges boarded the vessel several times to hold on-site meetings, cared about the crew's living conditions and vessel safety, urged the auction company to increase publicity efforts, and strictly controlled each link including inspection, evaluation, and safety supervision, ensuring that the vessel inspection and evaluation reports objectively reflected the actual condition and value of the vessel, thereby smoothly advancing the judicial auction procedure. The "Misimu" was ultimately won by a German shipping company at a price of RMB 39.9 million. At the end of December 2013, the court rendered judgments supporting the claims of the 11 crew members. The enforcement department promptly began distributing the crew's wages, allocating RMB 1.63 million from the auction price as labor remuneration for the 11 Ukrainian crew members on a priority basis.

(2) Judgment

Through the auction, the Shanghai Maritime Court ultimately had the vessel "Misimu" won by a German shipping company at RMB 39.9 million. After the successful auction, the judges first considered the priority payment of the crew's labor remuneration. On December 18, 2013, the Shanghai Maritime Court ruled that the 11 Ukrainian crew members, including the 6 who had returned earlier, should receive a total of RMB 1.63 million in labor remuneration from the auction proceeds.

(3) Typical Significance

This case is a typical foreign-related crew labor contract dispute. The Shanghai Maritime Court followed international practices and lawfully exercised its judicial power, not only equally protecting the lawful rights and interests of the foreign parties but also making foreign crew members feel the warmth of China's judiciary through humanistic care. The fair and efficient conclusion of the case was affirmed and thanked by the Consulate of Ukraine in Shanghai, establishing a good image of the Shanghai International Shipping Center externally.

The establishment of the Shanghai Pilot Free Trade Zone is a major decision by the Central Committee of the Communist Party and the State Council to coordinate both domestic and international situations, to align with global economic and trade development trends, and to open up more proactively to the outside world. It is a significant national strategy and also a major opportunity for Shanghai to accelerate the construction of "four centers" and to expedite the realization of "innovation-driven development and transformation of the development model." The construction of the Pilot Free Trade Zone will inevitably generate new demands for maritime judicial protection. The Shanghai Maritime Court will face new opportunities and challenges with the service and protection concept of "rule of law, marketization, and internationalization." That is, to properly resolve relevant litigated disputes within the framework of the rule of law using legal thinking and methods, to strengthen judicial transparency, to unify the application of law, to standardize discretionary acts, to provide stable judicial expectations for trade activities within the zone, to play the maritime judiciary's due role in building a rule-of-law business environment, and to promote the decisive role of the market in resource allocation in the shipping field through lawful adjudication. Adhere to the equal protection of litigation rights and lawful interests of Chinese and foreign parties in accordance with the law, follow international practices, common practices, and trading standards, and demonstrate the good international image of the Pilot Free Trade Zone.

IX. Wang Yongping Environmental Pollution Case

(1) Basic Facts

In early August 2013, without environmental protection approval procedures and pollution prevention equipment, the defendant Wang Yongping unlawfully engaged in electroplating processing and chrome plating of air conditioner brackets in a rented house in Yagucheng Village, Xiongzhou Town, Xiong County, and directly discharged the wastewater from the production process into a seepage pit outside the yard. Testing revealed that the water samples from the electroplating tank and the seepage pit contained toxic and hazardous substances. The defendant Wang Yongping's processing site was near agricultural land and residential areas.

(2) Judgment

The Xiong County People's Court of Hebei Province, in its first-instance judgment on December 19, 2013, held that: The defendant Wang Yongping, in violation of the state's laws and regulations on environmental protection and water pollution prevention, unlawfully set up a small electroplating stall explicitly prohibited by the state, and directly discharged wastewater containing toxic substances into a seepage pit. According to Article 1(4) of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Criminal Cases of Environmental Pollution, his conduct constituted the crime of environmental pollution. The defendant Wang Yongping's discharge of toxic substances near a residential area should be considered as an aggravating circumstance for sentencing, but he voluntarily confessed to the crime, which is a mitigating circumstance for sentencing. Accordingly, he was sentenced to one year and six months of imprisonment for the crime of environmental pollution and fined RMB 30,000.

(3) Typical Significance

To fully leverage the judicial function, the Supreme People's Court, in collaboration with relevant authorities, jointly issued the Interpretation on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Criminal Cases of Environmental Pollution on June 17, 2013. Based on legal provisions and legislative spirit, and considering practical difficulties in handling criminal environmental pollution cases such as evidence collection, identification, and determination, the Interpretation set new standards for conviction and sentencing of environmental pollution crimes, further intensifying the crackdown and tightening the criminal law net. The promulgation and implementation of the Interpretation played an important role in strengthening environmental protection, safeguarding the people's life, health, and property safety, and advancing the construction of a beautiful China. This case is a typical example of applying the Interpretation after its issuance by the Supreme People's Court and has a demonstrative effect on the adjudication of similar environmental pollution cases in the future.

X. China Environmental Protection Federation v. Wuxi Lihu Huishan Scenic Area Management Committee — Ecological Environment Tort Case

(1) Basic Facts

The Wuxi Zoo and Taihu Happy Park (hereinafter referred to as "Happy Park") were key municipal ecological environment projects and "practical projects for the people" undertaken by the Wuxi Lihu Huishan Scenic Area Management Committee (hereinafter referred to as "Scenic Area Management Committee"). During the construction of this project, the Scenic Area Management Committee changed the use of part of the forest land without approval, with 3,677 square meters being used to build sightseeing elevators and fire water tanks.

(2) Judgment

The Binhu District People's Court of Wuxi, Jiangsu Province, after trial, held that: The Scenic Area Management Committee had not obtained approval procedures for changing the use of forest land when developing and constructing the project, constituting the fact of occupying forest land. The change of use of forest land caused damage to the ecological environment, and the Scenic Area Management Committee should bear corresponding civil tort liability. According to law, the act of changing the use of forest land should be ordered to restore the original state within a time limit. However, considering that the fire water tanks and sightseeing elevators also served as escape and emergency access routes and were necessary components of Happy Park, involving significant social public interests, directly restoring the original state might result in a waste of social resources. If restoration in situ is truly difficult, restoration may be carried out at an alternative site to achieve or exceed the original ecological capacity level as much as possible. The selection of the alternative restoration site should be determined based on the principle of the closest connection to the original infringed location and the economic reliability of the restoration plan. Ultimately, considering comprehensive factors such as the feasibility of the replanting plan, the reasonableness of the choice of seedlings, and the convenience of forest maintenance, the court ruled that the replanting plan at the Yangwan plot in Binhu District, Wuxi, would be the final plan for restoring the forest land in this case, and confirmed and approved the alternative restoration plan submitted by the defendant. In March and April 2013, the Scenic Area Management Committee invested nearly RMB 800,000 to reclaim and plant 7,000 square meters of urban green space at the Yangwan plot, with the court participating in the entire process of supervision and acceptance, and also supervising the Scenic Area Management Committee in carrying out the defect period maintenance of the trees (one year).

(3) Typical Significance

This case is an environmental public interest litigation initiated by the China Environmental Protection Federation. Where a construction project occupies and changes the use of forest land without approval, causing damage to the ecological environment, the construction unit shall bear corresponding civil liability. Since the amount of ecological damage compensation due to the reduction of tree area cannot be quantified and assessed, and restoring the original state in situ may cause significant waste of social wealth, the people's court may rule that the construction unit restore the ecological capacity through alternative replanting at another site.

XI. Shanghai Zhou A Robbery Case (Post-Sentencing Education for Juvenile Offender)

(1) Basic Facts

In the afternoon of October 9, 2002, the defendant Zhou A, together with co-defendant Deng Xiaoyong (already sentenced), after premeditation, went to the temporary residence of the victim Pan Hongliang at Room 403, No. 10, Lane 380, Honggu Road, Shanghai. They bound the victim Pan Hongliang's hands and feet with packing tape, threatened him with a knife, robbed him of RMB 650, a Bird brand S2000 mobile phone valued at RMB 1,760, and a bank savings card, and coerced the victim into providing the savings card password. Subsequently, they used the savings card to withdraw RMB 1,200 from a bank. Zhou A then left Shanghai, drifted to places such as Dongguan, Guangdong, and lived in fear for over five years. During this period, his co-defendant was arrested by the police and sentenced to ten years of imprisonment.

In December 2007, Zhou A left a message on the "China Fallen Youth Hotline" founded by volunteer Wang Jinyun in Shenzhen, pouring out his inner distress and depression. On March 21, 2008, the defendant Zhou A finally mustered up the courage, accompanied by Wang Jinyun, to surrender to the Shanghai police.

(2) Judgment

The court held that the defendant Zhou A, with the purpose of illegal possession, in collusion with others, forcibly entered a residence and used violence to rob a citizen's property. His conduct constituted the crime of robbery and he should bear criminal responsibility according to law. At the time of the crime, the defendant Zhou A was under the age of 18, had the circumstance of voluntary surrender, showed genuine repentance, and was subject to a mitigated punishment according to law. The defendant Zhou A voluntarily confessed to the crime and made restitution for the victim's economic losses. The facts charged by the prosecutorial authority were clear, and the evidence was conclusive and sufficient. The defense counsel's opinion regarding sentencing Zhou A to a suspended sentence was lawful and well-founded and was adopted; the defense counsel's opinion that Zhou A's conduct constituted ordinary robbery and that he was an accomplice was not adopted based on the facts and circumstances of this case. The defendant Zhou A's subjective malignity and criminal circumstances in the joint crime were relatively minor, which was fully considered in sentencing. To protect the personal and property rights of citizens, in accordance with Article 263(1), Article 17(1) and (3), Article 67(1), Article 72, Article 73(2) and (3), Article 53, and Article 64 of the Criminal Law of the PRC, and Article 1 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Specific Application of Law in Handling Cases of Voluntary Surrender and Meritorious Service, the court sentenced the defendant Zhou A to three years of imprisonment for the crime of robbery, suspended for three years, and fined RMB 2,000.

After the judgment took effect, the Juvenile Division of the Changning District Court, with the cooperation and support of the Shanghai Volunteers Association for Education and Assistance, arranged for Zhou A to work in a caring enterprise in Shanghai while undergoing community correction. After he initially adapted to society, in September of the same year, with the consent of the Shanghai community correction department, Zhou A returned to his hometown in Hanyin County, Shaanxi, to continue community correction. In October 2008, with the care and support of his family and the assistance organization, Zhou A raised over RMB 100,000 and opened the "Car Decoration World Car Beauty Center," which was developed as a community correction placement and assistance base. In April 2011, with the support of the local government, the Sanshi Automobile Service Co., Ltd., with an investment of over RMB 4 million and covering an area of over 5,000 square meters, was established. Upon arrangement by the relevant local authorities, Zhou A's company was designated as the Xin Hang Home placement and assistance base. To date, it has accepted over 20 released prisoners to work in the company and has facilitated their education and supervision by relevant authorities. Zhou A also used his own experience to persuade three fugitives to surrender. Zhou A's above performance received widespread praise from society. In 2012, he was named "Top Ten Outstanding Youth of Hanyin County" and "Advanced Individual in Comprehensive Social Management Work." In November 2011, the CCTV program "News Documentary" reported in detail on the "Xin Hang Home" placement and assistance base in Hanyin County under the title "Summons Under the Sun," attracting attention from the province and the whole country.

(3) Typical Significance

Post-sentencing education for minors, especially migrant minors, has long been a difficult issue troubling juvenile court judges. Post-sentencing education for minors should fully leverage social forces to form a joint effort in education and assistance, achieving the goal of helping them help themselves.

This case demonstrates seamless connection in post-sentencing education. First, the relay between the juvenile court and the volunteers association for education and assistance. The juvenile court fully utilized social resources, actively cooperated with the Shanghai Judicial Bureau's Volunteers Association for Education and Assistance, and, after securing a caring enterprise, boldly applied non-custodial penalties to migrant minors, allowing them to work while undergoing community correction. Second, the relay between the Shanghai community correction organization and the community correction organization of the minor's place of origin. Through the joint efforts of community correction organizations in Shanghai and Shaanxi, Zhou A was able to return to his hometown to start his own business, which was subsequently developed into a local assistance base, accepting offenders to give back to society.

The success of Zhou A's education and assistance was the result of the joint efforts of the Shenzhen volunteer assistance organization, the juvenile court, the Shanghai Volunteers Association for Education and Assistance, and the community correction departments in Shanghai and the local area. It also brings new inspiration for integrating forces in juvenile trials to carry out education and assistance for migrant minors.
